title: Hook a bed's side rail onto its headboard leg: both hooks into their slots at once, then drive it down until seated
instruction: Attach the side rail's loose end to the headboard post, fully seated.
context: Taking a wooden bed apart and putting it back together comes with almost every move, and moves are frequent (a US resident can expect to move 11.7 times in a lifetime, US Census Bureau). This queen bed, built to Woodworker's Journal's published plan, joins rails to legs with Rockler hook-in fasteners: two hooks on the rail's end go through two slots in the leg's plate and drop behind it, and their tapered throats wedge the joint, so the rail is tapped down to lock it. The far end rests on a helper support; the hands carry the near end (about 20 N) and keep it plumb, because both 4 mm hooks must meet their 6.35 mm slots at once, inside a 3.2 mm height window, while pressing towards the leg; then both drive the joint down its last 3 mm.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights in mm above the table top, which, extended level all round as a 2.6 x 3.6 m platform of the same colour, stands in for the bedroom floor. Bed: a solid-wood queen frame built to Woodworker's Journal's Greene & Greene-inspired queen bed plan (legs 70 x 35 mm), wood. Headboard (fixed): legs 978 mm tall, at x 0.265 to 0.335 (near leg) and 1.843 to 1.913 (far leg), y 0.070 to 0.105, joined by a 25 x 165 mm bottom rail 35 to 200 mm up, a 19 mm panel with five 50 mm battens, and a 35 x 76 mm top rail 882 to 958 mm up; the near leg's 70 mm face at y 0.070 faces the robot's right. Slotted plate of a Rockler 6 in x 5/8 in Heavy Duty Wrought Steel Bed Rail Fastener (item 28597): steel, 151 x 15.9 x 3.6 mm, flush in that face, centred on x 0.300, 42 to 193 mm up; two slots 6.35 mm wide and 25.4 mm tall (lower 69 to 95 mm up, upper 152 to 177 mm up), each with a hook mortise behind it 6.35 mm wide and 12.7 mm deep reaching 13 mm below the slot. Far side rail (fixed, already hooked onto the far leg): wood, 28.6 x 165 mm, 2.057 m, centred on x 1.878, 35 to 200 mm up, its far end on a 90 x 90 x 35 mm wood block. Footboard (fixed, not yet hooked on, 6 cm beyond the near rail's far end): legs 546 mm tall at the same x as the headboard's, y -2.112 to -2.077, with a bottom rail, panel and top rail like the headboard's, and slotted plates in both legs. On the floor inside the frame: the plan's six pine cross supports (19 x 114 x 1543 mm), stacked two high along y from -0.40 to -1.94 at x 0.92 to 1.27, and two 38 mm steel angle irons (2.03 m) at x 1.45 and 1.53. Near side rail (free): poplar, 28.6 mm thick, 165 mm tall, 2.057 m long, 4.4 kg, with the fastener's hook plate (steel, 151 x 15.9 x 3.6 mm) flush and centred in each end; the near end's two steel hooks are 4.0 mm thick, stand 11.1 mm out of the end and are 22.2 mm tall (a 12.7 mm neck and a 9.5 mm tip hanging below it, 4.0 mm clear of the end at the neck), their tops 129.5 and 46.9 mm above the rail's underside (82.5 mm apart). Seated, the rail is level, its underside 35 mm up, its end against the leg's face and the hooks' necks on the slots' bottoms. Helper support (fixed) under the near rail 10 cm from its far end (y -1.887): a 90 x 90 mm wood block carrying a 20 mm dowel across, its top 35 mm up, between two wood guide cheeks 12 mm thick reaching 85 mm up, 1.5 mm clear of the rail each side. Start: the near rail lies on the dowel and its near end's underside rests on the floor with its end 30 mm short of the leg's face and 25 mm towards the arms (end's underside centre at x 0.275, y 0.040), so it slopes 1.0 degree down to the floor. Distractors, loose on the floor, which scoring ignores: a ceramic coffee mug (114 x 90 x 80 mm, 0.30 kg) at x 0.62, y -0.36; a Phillips screwdriver (188 mm, 0.10 kg) at x 0.60, y -0.03; the assembly booklet (229 x 170 x 10 mm, 0.12 kg) at x 0.86, y -0.30. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read at each of the two hooks: s, the rail end's height above its seated line (marked on the leg at setup with the rail fully seated; negative when below it); gap, the rail's end face to the leg's face at that hook's height (negative when past it); e, the hook's sideways offset from its slot's centre (the rail end's centre from the slots' centre line marked on the leg). A hook is in (through its slot and dropped behind the plate) when its gap is more than -1.5 mm and at most 7.5 mm, its s more than -1.5 mm and at most 9.5 mm, and its e at most 2 mm either way; it is seated when it is in with s and gap each within 1 mm of zero. 0 if at any time the rail end is dropped (it falls faster than 0.5 m/s, about a 1.3 cm free fall, while every point of both grippers is more than 2 cm from the rail) or forced into the leg (its end 1.5 mm or more past the leg's face, a hook in its slot 1.5 mm or more below its seated height, or a hook 1.5 mm or more past the leg's face more than 2.7 mm off its slot's centre, that is, pushed into the plate). Otherwise: 1.0 (success) when both hooks are seated for 3 s running, with every point of both grippers at least 3 cm from the rail and the rail still (under 1 cm/s and 0.1 rad/s); else at the end 0.75 if both hooks are in with s 4.5 mm or less at both (hung on the wedge fit but not driven home); 0.5 if both hooks are in; 0.25 if one hook is in; 0 otherwise. So a rail end left on the floor (s about -35 mm) or slid beside the leg (e over 40 mm) scores 0, and doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lift the rail's near end straight up about 15 mm to free the hooks, draw it back from the leg and set its end on the floor at its tape marks (end 30 mm short of the leg, 25 mm towards the robot); its far end stays on the helper support's dowel. The wedged hooks need a firm upward pull or a tap from below to release.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics. Real-size queen frame from a published plan; headboard, footboard and far rail fixed. Near rail 2.06 m, 4.4 kg poplar (the plan uses mahogany), its far end on a helper support (dowel between cheeks). Real-size convex hooks and slots; the wedge fit over the last 3 mm is a stop giving only to over 16 N per hook (estimated). Floor: the table top extended. No grain, rail twist or frame racking; friction uniform per part.
